title: Aerospace & Defense
summary: Precision manufacturing, MRO (Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul), and specialized services with high barriers to entry and sticky government or prime-contractor relationships.
businessModel: Manufacturing highly engineered components or providing specialized maintenance and engineering services to OEMs and government entities.
revenueModel: Long-term, programmatic contracts (often multi-year), aftermarket spare parts sales, and recurring MRO service revenue.
costStructure: Highly skilled labor (machinists, engineers), specialized raw materials (exotic alloys), capital equipment (CNC machines), and rigorous compliance/QA overhead.
whyPeLikesIt: Unparalleled revenue visibility through multi-year government budgets, massive barriers to entry via ITAR and AS9100 certifications, and the 'sticky' nature of being designed into a platform for decades.
investmentThesis: Consolidate fragmented, highly specialized 'mom-and-pop' machine shops to create a scaled Tier 2/Tier 3 supplier that can offer full sub-assemblies to Tier 1 Primes, driving multiple expansion through scale.
diligenceQuestions: What percentage of revenue is 'sole-source' versus competitively bid?
How exposed is the backlog to specific defense platforms or commercial aircraft build rates?
Are all ITAR, NIST, and AS9100 certifications current and auditable?
operationalIssues: Poor throughput and low OEE in the machine shop.
Inefficient capture management leading to low win rates on bids.
Over-reliance on outdated ERP systems and tribal knowledge for quoting.
valueCreationLevers: Pricing power on sole-source or aftermarket parts
Professionalized business development and capture management
Strategic add-ons to acquire adjacent capabilities (e.g., adding composites to metal fabrication)
aiOpportunities: AI-driven quoting engines based on historical machine times and material costs.
Predictive maintenance for critical CNC machinery.
Automated inspection using computer vision to improve First Pass Yield.
risks: Defense budget cuts or program cancellations.
Severe shortages of highly skilled machinists and engineers.
Cybersecurity vulnerabilities leading to loss of clearance or contracts.
hundredDayPlan: Assess and upgrade cybersecurity posture (CMMC compliance).
Implement daily shop-floor huddles tracking OEE and OTD.
Standardize the quoting and estimating process.
exitReadiness: Strong, diversified backlog across multiple long-term platforms.
Bulletproof compliance and quality management records.
Demonstrated ability to deliver fully integrated sub-assemblies rather than isolated parts.

articleSections.title: Consolidating the Fragmented Supply Chain
body: The Aerospace & Defense (A&D) supply chain is historically highly fragmented, characterized by thousands of founder-owned, highly specialized machine shops. Tier 1 'Primes' like Boeing, Lockheed Martin, or Raytheon are increasingly seeking to rationalize their supplier base. They prefer to deal with a few scaled Tier 2 suppliers who can provide complete, integrated sub-assemblies rather than managing the logistical nightmare of buying thousands of individual widgets from tiny shops. The Private Equity playbook capitalizes on this macro trend: acquire a platform company with essential certifications and aggressively execute M&A to build a comprehensive 'One-Stop-Shop' for the Primes.

Value creation in this space is heavily driven by multiple expansion generated through scale and expanded capabilities. A $5M EBITDA machine shop producing only metal fasteners might trade at 6x EBITDA, but a $50M EBITDA integrated supplier boasting capabilities across metal machining, advanced composites, proprietary coatings, and final assembly will command 12-14x EBITDA. The Operating Partner's critical role is to integrate these acquisitions seamlessly, ensuring that strict quality management systems (like AS9100) and cybersecurity protocols (CMMC) are unified across all facilities, thereby protecting the platform from jeopardizing existing prime contracts.

To achieve this, we implement rigorous supply chain consolidation frameworks during the first 100 days post-acquisition. We aggressively eliminate redundant overhead, centralize the procurement of exotic raw materials (like titanium or Inconel) to secure volume discounts, and standardize the ERP systems across the newly formed enterprise. A successfully integrated A&D platform becomes an indispensable, deeply embedded partner to the Primes, generating highly predictable, multi-decade revenue streams that strategic buyers covet at exit.
articleSections.callout: In A&D, Primes want to buy completed assemblies, not isolated parts. Aggressive consolidation is the direct path to becoming an indispensable, high-multiple Tier 2 partner.

articleSections.title: Throughput Optimization and the Shop Floor
body: Manufacturing profitability in A&D is definitively dictated by 'Overall Equipment Effectiveness' (OEE) and 'First Pass Yield.' Many founder-owned machine shops operate with significant, hidden inefficiencies. It is common to find that actual spindle time on multi-million dollar 5-axis CNC machines is less than 40% due to chaotic scheduling, missing raw materials, and excessively long setup times. We initiate margin expansion by implementing rigorous Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma principles directly on the shop floor.

By focusing heavily on 'SMED' (Single-Minute Exchange of Die) methodologies to radically reduce changeover times, and reorganizing the shop floor layout for optimal, continuous flow, we can effectively unlock 'hidden capacity.' Increasing OEE from 40% to 65% allows the business to process significantly more revenue without the need to deploy additional CapEx for new machinery. Furthermore, we institute strict daily management cadences—implementing visual management boards that track 'On-Time Delivery' (OTD) and defect rates on a shift-by-shift basis, demanding root-cause analysis for any variance.

The financial and strategic impact of this operational discipline is two-fold. First, moving First Pass Yield from 92% to 99% protects the gross margin by eliminating the exorbitant costs of rework, scrap, and expedited freight. Second, and perhaps more importantly, elevating OTD from 85% to a sustained 98%+ dramatically improves the company's 'Supplier Scorecard' with the Primes. A top-tier scorecard is the prerequisite for winning larger, programmatic work, turning operational excellence directly into top-line revenue growth.

articleSections.title: Professionalizing Capture Management and Bidding
body: Growth in defense contracting requires navigating Byzantine, multi-year government procurement cycles. Many target companies in the middle market rely entirely on passive relationships, legacy contracts, or the 'tribal knowledge' of the founder for quoting new work. We professionalize the 'Capture Management' and business development process from day one. This involves recruiting seasoned executives who possess deep relationships within the DoD and implementing robust CRM systems to track the pipeline of upcoming Requests for Proposals (RFPs) years before they are officially released.

Equally important to winning bids is standardizing the internal estimating and quoting engine. We implement sophisticated, data-driven quoting models that accurately capture historical machine times, precise material yield/waste factors, and fully burdened overhead rates, effectively moving the organization away from 'gut feel' pricing. This analytical rigor ensures that the business is not just winning bids to drive top-line vanity metrics, but is securing structurally profitable contracts, meticulously avoiding the 'Winner's Curse' prevalent in fixed-price manufacturing.

We measure success in this area by tracking the 'Win Rate' (Capture Ratio) and the 'Book-to-Bill Ratio.' A Book-to-Bill ratio consistently over 1.2x signals robust future revenue growth. For a $100M A&D platform, increasing the Win Rate on profitable bids by just 10% can add $15M-$20M to the backlog. The Operating Partner ensures that the sales and manufacturing teams are perfectly aligned, guaranteeing that the company only bids on work that matches its optimal machine capabilities and margin profile.

articleSections.title: Pricing Power in Aftermarket and Sole-Source Scenarios
body: While new-build OEM manufacturing contracts provide critical volume, they are often fiercely competitive and carry lower initial margins. The true EBITDA expansion engine in A&D resides in the 'Aftermarket'—the sale of replacement spare parts and MRO (Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul) services. Components that are successfully designed into an aircraft platform that will fly for 30 years enjoy a highly captive market. During diligence, we conduct deep-dive margin analytics to specifically identify 'Sole-Source' parts where our platform holds the proprietary IP or is the only FDA/FAA certified manufacturer.

Because the engineering and regulatory costs of re-qualifying a new, unproven supplier are astronomically high for the Prime, these sole-source positions carry immense, often untapped pricing power. We systematically implement strategic price increases on these proprietary, highly specialized components. Because the cost of the individual part is typically a microscopic fraction of the total aircraft cost, Primes will generally absorb these increases to ensure supply chain continuity.

Even a seemingly modest 5-7% price realization on a portfolio of sole-source aftermarket parts drops almost entirely to the bottom line, radically transforming the profitability profile of the acquired platform. We expect the management team to utilize advanced pricing software to continuously test elasticity and ensure that the value delivered by the platform is accurately captured in its margins. This pricing discipline is a hallmark of a highly sophisticated, exit-ready defense asset.
